refuted.point: StudioContext type includes 'school-console' as a sixth context value ('commons' | 'network' | 'workbench' | 'records' | 'intelligence' | 'school-console')
refuted.why: Charter §4 hard navigation constraints: 'No sixth primary module unless a genuinely independent user job cannot fit into the five.' User ruling #2: 'Make the shell genuinely minimal. Five modules, one workspace, one shared graph.' School Console is explicitly an operational boundary under Workbench, not a separate module or context. Adding it to StudioContext makes it a sixth rail item or parallel navigation target, violating the five-module constraint.
refuted.fix: Remove 'school-console' from StudioContext type. School Console should only appear as a Workbench sidebar destination, not as a StudioContext value. The route /workspace/workbench/school-console handles it without polluting the module context enum.

refuted.point: Records module page head has a three-way lens switcher (Canon | Annals | Roll) as primary navigation in the page head
refuted.why: Charter §5: 'They must remain conceptually distinct while being navigable together.' User ruling #3: 'Do not force every page into an identical four-metric header. Establish one hierarchy and let the information determine how much of it appears. Consistency must not become ceremony.' A prominent lens switcher in the page head risks becoming a 'workspace-within-workspace' (Charter §4: 'No workspace-within-workspace architecture unless an actual permission or operational boundary requires it') and ritualizes the page head across different jobs.
refuted.fix: Make lens switching contextual and lightweight — e.g., a segmented control or tab bar within the Records module's main surface, not a page-head fixture. Deep links via ?lens=annals|roll are fine. The page head should show Canon/Annals/Roll metrics only when they drive decisions, not as a permanent header element.

refuted.point: Page head shows metrics on Records (Canon head, Annals event count, Roll entry count) and Workbench (simulation stage) as a sign-off test
refuted.why: User ruling #3 explicitly: 'Do not force every page into an identical four-metric header.' Charter §8 anti-slop: 'Decorative metrics with no operational meaning.' Metrics in page heads must be decision-driving, not decorative. Records Canon head count, Annals event count, and Roll entry count are inventory metrics — they don't inherently drive decisions unless the user is actively triaging. Workbench simulation stage is operational but shouldn't be forced into a header ritual.
refuted.fix: Remove 'page head shows metrics' as a universal requirement. Only show metrics where they directly inform the immediate decision (e.g., Workbench simulation stage during active simulation, Roll evidence gaps when substantiating a claim). Make metric presence conditional on the job, not the module.

refuted.point: Sidebar shows 'context destinations within the active module' — e.g., Network shows People/Institutions/Capabilities as separate sidebar items
refuted.why: Charter §4 hard constraint: 'No duplicate navigation systems inside individual pages.' Current repo-facts show Network module already has contexts: people, institutions, capabilities. Making these sidebar destinations creates a second navigation layer (rail = module, sidebar = sub-module) that duplicates the module-switching job. The charter says rail = module switcher (one job), sidebar = context navigator within module (one job) — but if 'context navigator' means 'switch between People/Institutions/Capabilities', that's effectively module switching by another name.
refuted.fix: Sidebar should show *contextual* destinations (filters, views, actions relevant to the current entity/work), not *structural* sub-modules. People/Institutions/Capabilities are better handled as inline tabs, filters, or view modes within the Network module's main surface, not as persistent sidebar navigation items that mirror the rail's job.

refuted.point: Inspector shows 'selected record/event context' and Dock shows 'change-set/evidence/reconciliation for active context' as separate panes for all modules
refuted.why: Charter §4: 'Shell chrome must contain no competing navigation systems: topbar, rail, sidebar, inspector, and dock each have exactly one job.' Current repo-facts: 'Current WorkspaceShell.tsx has inspector + dock + sidebar all showing overlapping links. StudioNavigation.tsx rail + sidebar duplicate module switching.' The proposal keeps inspector and dock as permanent shell chrome for all modules, but repo-facts confirm 'NOT present: record-level inspector, change-set/ledger dock'. Only Records and Intelligence genuinely need persistent inspection (Charter §4: 'Records may be a primary destination, but its underlying functions... must also appear contextually throughout the product'). Forcing inspector/dock on Commons, Network, Workbench creates empty chrome.
refuted.fix: Make inspector and dock *contextual* — they appear only when a record/event/change-set is selected and only for modules that need them (Records, Intelligence, Workbench during simulation). Hide them entirely for Commons and Network. This avoids 'competing navigation systems' and empty chrome.

refuted.point: Fork glyph appears in Records lens=Canon when viewing a proposed change-set, Workbench when simulation diverges, and dock/commit list
refuted.why: User ruling #1: 'The fork glyph may remain as an identity element.' Charter §8: 'The surveyor's grid, evidence markers, branch/fork glyph, and instrument readouts are signature devices. Spend visual emphasis selectively.' The proposal correctly restricts fork glyph to proposed change-sets, not as environment switcher. However, placing it in 'dock/commit list showing proposed commits' risks making it a persistent chrome element rather than a contextual identity marker on the specific divergent record.
refuted.fix: Restrict fork glyph to the specific proposed change-set record view (in Records Canon lens) and the active Workbench simulation surface when diverged. Remove from generic dock/commit list — that becomes a navigation element, not an identity device.

refuted.point: Build order step 7: 'Refactor WorkspaceShell.tsx: single rail (5 modules), sidebar (context destinations), inspector (record/event only), dock (change-set/evidence/reconciliation)'
refuted.why: This step locks in the problematic inspector/dock as permanent shell chrome for all modules (see point above). The charter says inspector/dock each have 'exactly one job' — but that job is *contextual inspection*, not *permanent pane*. Making them always-present shell chrome violates 'no competing navigation systems' and creates the empty-chrome problem repo-facts already identifies.
refuted.fix: Refactor WorkspaceShell.tsx to make inspector and dock *conditional* components that mount only when a record/event/change-set is selected in a module that supports it. Default shell = topbar + rail + sidebar + main. Inspector/dock = ephemeral overlays or side-sheets triggered by selection.

refuted.point: Sign-off test: 'Charter's twelve never-equate distinctions are visible in changeset state labels (e.g., PROPOSED≠ACCEPTED, IN_REVIEW≠AUTHORIZED)'
refuted.why: Charter §3 lists 12 never-equate distinctions. The proposal's state machine (DRAFT → PROPOSED → IN_REVIEW → (PENDING_AUTHORIZATION | PENDING_EVIDENCE) → ACCEPTED | REJECTED | AMENDED) only surfaces ~4 of them explicitly. Claiming all 12 are 'visible in changeset state labels' overstates what a state machine can convey — many distinctions (Person≠Asset, Capability≠Credential, Reputation≠Trust, Record≠Truth, Visibility≠Permission, AI suggestion≠institutional decision) are domain modeling concerns, not changeset state labels.
refuted.fix: Revise sign-off test: changeset state machine must correctly model the work-progression distinctions (Claim≠Evidence, Recommendation≠Approval≠Authorization, Execution≠Acceptance, Acceptance≠Settlement). The other 8 distinctions must be preserved in domain types, permission models, and evidence presentation — not forced into changeset labels.
